+from collections import defaultdict
+from dataclasses import dataclass
 from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
+from decimal import Decimal
+from typing import Iterable
 from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Sale:
+    order_id: str
+    store_id: str
+    occurred_at: datetime
+    gross: Decimal
+    tax: Decimal
+    refunded: bool = False
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class DailyTotals:
+    day: date
+    store_id: str
+    order_count: int
+    gross: Decimal
+    tax: Decimal
+    refunds: Decimal
 
 
 def utc_bounds(day: date, zone_name: str) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
     zone = ZoneInfo(zone_name)
     start = datetime.combine(day, time.min, zone).astimezone(timezone.utc)
-    end = datetime.combine(day + timedelta(days=1), time.min, zone).astimezone(timezone.utc)
+    end = start + timedelta(days=1)
     return start, end
+
+
+def validate_sale(sale: Sale) -> None:
+    if sale.occurred_at.tzinfo is None:
+        raise ValueError("sale timestamp must be timezone-aware")
+    if sale.gross < 0 or sale.tax < 0:
+        raise ValueError("sale values cannot be negative")
+    if sale.tax > sale.gross:
+        raise ValueError("tax cannot exceed gross")
+
+
+def belongs_to_day(sale: Sale, day: date, zone_name: str) -> bool:
+    start, end = utc_bounds(day, zone_name)
+    instant = sale.occurred_at.astimezone(timezone.utc)
+    return start <= instant < end
+
+
+def calculate_totals(
+    sales: Iterable[Sale],
+    day: date,
+    store_id: str,
+    zone_name: str,
+) -> DailyTotals:
+    gross = Decimal("0")
+    tax = Decimal("0")
+    refunds = Decimal("0")
+    count = 0
+    for sale in sales:
+        validate_sale(sale)
+        if sale.store_id != store_id or not belongs_to_day(sale, day, zone_name):
+            continue
+        if sale.refunded:
+            refunds += sale.gross
+        else:
+            gross += sale.gross
+            tax += sale.tax
+            count += 1
+    return DailyTotals(day, store_id, count, gross, tax, refunds)
+
+
+def net_total(totals: DailyTotals) -> Decimal:
+    return totals.gross - totals.refunds
+
+
+def average_order(totals: DailyTotals) -> Decimal:
+    if totals.order_count == 0:
+        return Decimal("0")
+    return totals.gross / Decimal(totals.order_count)
+
+
+def totals_by_store(
+    sales: Iterable[Sale],
+    day: date,
+    store_zones: dict[str, str],
+) -> dict[str, DailyTotals]:
+    records = list(sales)
+    return {
+        store_id: calculate_totals(records, day, store_id, zone_name)
+        for store_id, zone_name in store_zones.items()
+    }
+
+
+def aggregate_week(
+    sales: Iterable[Sale],
+    first_day: date,
+    store_id: str,
+    zone_name: str,
+) -> list[DailyTotals]:
+    records = list(sales)
+    return [
+        calculate_totals(records, first_day + timedelta(days=offset), store_id, zone_name)
+        for offset in range(7)
+    ]
+
+
+def monthly_gross(daily: Iterable[DailyTotals]) -> dict[tuple[int, int], Decimal]:
+    result: dict[tuple[int, int], Decimal] = defaultdict(lambda: Decimal("0"))
+    for totals in daily:
+        result[(totals.day.year, totals.day.month)] += totals.gross
+    return dict(result)
+
+
+def monthly_refunds(daily: Iterable[DailyTotals]) -> dict[tuple[int, int], Decimal]:
+    result: dict[tuple[int, int], Decimal] = defaultdict(lambda: Decimal("0"))
+    for totals in daily:
+        result[(totals.day.year, totals.day.month)] += totals.refunds
+    return dict(result)
+
+
+def encode_totals(totals: DailyTotals) -> dict[str, object]:
+    return {
+        "date": totals.day.isoformat(),
+        "store": totals.store_id,
+        "orders": totals.order_count,
+        "gross": str(totals.gross),
+        "tax": str(totals.tax),
+        "refunds": str(totals.refunds),
+        "net": str(net_total(totals)),
+    }
+
+
+def merge_totals(left: DailyTotals, right: DailyTotals) -> DailyTotals:
+    if (left.day, left.store_id) != (right.day, right.store_id):
+        raise ValueError("totals must refer to the same store and day")
+    return DailyTotals(
+        day=left.day,
+        store_id=left.store_id,
+        order_count=left.order_count + right.order_count,
+        gross=left.gross + right.gross,
+        tax=left.tax + right.tax,
+        refunds=left.refunds + right.refunds,
+    )
+
+
+def fiscal_quarter(day: date) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    return day.year, ((day.month - 1) // 3) + 1
+
+
+def report_label(day: date, store_id: str) -> str:
+    return f"{store_id}:{day.isoformat()}"
+
+
+def report_range(days: Iterable[date], zone_name: str) -> list[tuple[datetime, datetime]]:
+    return [utc_bounds(day, zone_name) for day in days]

from datetime import date, datetime, time, timedelta, timezone
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo


def utc_bounds(day: date, zone_name: str) -> tuple[datetime, datetime]:
    zone = ZoneInfo(zone_name)
    start = datetime.combine(day, time.min, zone).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    end = datetime.combine(day + timedelta(days=1), time.min, zone).astimezone(timezone.utc)
    return start, end

ground_truth.rationale: A local calendar day can be 23 or 25 hours. Adding 24 hours to its UTC start includes part of the next day or misses the last hour on DST transition dates, corrupting daily totals.
